o: Compute each team's rank before (by points DESC, name ASC) and after adding points_change (same tie-break), then report old_rank minus new_rank. Example 1: Algeria jumps from rank 3 to 2 (+1), Croatia slips from 2 to 3 (-1) due to the lexicographic tie with Algeria, Senegal and New Zealand stay at 0. Window functions RANK() over the two orderings, joined on team_id, solve this cleanly.
k: Rank ordering: points DESC, then name ASC.
rank_diff = old_rank - new_rank (positive means the team moved up).

a.i: Derive old and new rankings with RANK() window functions in CTEs, join them per team, and subtract.
s: CTE old: rank TeamPoints by points DESC, name ASC.
CTE new: join PointsChange, rank by points + points_change DESC, name ASC.
Join on team_id and select old_rank - new_rank AS rank_diff.

c.python:
WITH old_r AS (
    SELECT team_id, name,
           RANK() OVER (ORDER BY points DESC, name ASC) AS r
    FROM TeamPoints
),
new_r AS (
    SELECT t.team_id, t.name,
           RANK() OVER (ORDER BY t.points + p.points_change DESC, t.name ASC) AS r
    FROM TeamPoints t
    JOIN PointsChange p ON t.team_id = p.team_id
)
SELECT o.team_id, o.name, o.r - n.r AS rank_diff
FROM old_r o
JOIN new_r n ON o.team_id = n.team_id;

a.t: O(k log k) for k teams — two sorts for the window rankings plus a join

w: Use RANK() (not ROW_NUMBER or DENSE_RANK) so tied points share a rank exactly as specified. Direction check: rank_diff = old - new, so gaining ranks yields positive values. Follow-up: return only teams whose rank changed — add a WHERE o.r <> n.r filter.
